abstract: BACKGROUND: Statins are widely used to lower LDL cholesterol. RESULTS: In this randomized controlled trial of 1200 patients, statin therapy reduced major cardiovascular events by 28% over 5 years compared to placebo (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.61-0.85). The absolute risk reduction was 4.2%. No significant increase in myopathy was observed.
title: Statin therapy and cardiovascular event reduction: a randomized controlled trial

abstract: BACKGROUND: Metformin is first-line treatment for type 2 diabetes. RESULTS: Metformin reduced HbA1c by 1.5% versus 0.3% in the placebo group (p < 0.001) in 800 adults with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes over 12 months. Weight was stable in the metformin group and increased by 2.1 kg in placebo. Gastrointestinal adverse events occurred in 18% of metformin patients.
title: Metformin versus placebo for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes

abstract: BACKGROUND: Aspirin has been evaluated for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease. RESULTS: In 12,000 adults without prior cardiovascular events, aspirin did not significantly reduce first myocardial infarction (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.88-1.05) and increased major gastrointestinal bleeding by 44% over 7 years. Net benefit was absent in the low-cardiovascular-risk population studied.
title: Aspirin for primary cardiovascular prevention: net harm in low-risk adults

abstract: BACKGROUND: Corticosteroids are used in septic shock management. RESULTS: Hydrocortisone 200 mg/day for 7 days in 800 mechanically ventilated septic shock patients did not reduce 90-day mortality compared to placebo (29.3% vs 32.5%, RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.79-1.03). Time to reversal of shock was significantly shorter in the hydrocortisone group (3 vs 4 days, p = 0.01).
title: Hydrocortisone in septic shock: mortality and shock reversal outcomes

abstract: BACKGROUND: PD-1 inhibitors have shown efficacy in non-small cell lung cancer. RESULTS: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone in 600 treatment-naive patients with metastatic NSCLC showed improved overall survival (median 21.9 vs 14.2 months, HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.50-0.77). PFS was also prolonged. Immune-related adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 17% of combination patients.
title: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy for metastatic non-small cell lung cancer

abstract: BACKGROUND: SSRIs are standard treatment for major depressive disorder. RESULTS: Escitalopram 10-20 mg/day compared to placebo in 450 patients with moderate-to-severe MDD showed response rates of 63% versus 38% at 8 weeks (NNT 4.0). Remission was achieved by 45% versus 26%. Nausea was the most common adverse event (22% escitalopram vs 8% placebo). Sexual dysfunction was reported in 14% versus 4%.
title: Escitalopram versus placebo for major depressive disorder: efficacy and tolerability

abstract: BACKGROUND: Beta-blockers are used in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. RESULTS: Carvedilol 25 mg twice daily versus placebo in 1094 patients with chronic HFrEF (EF < 35%) reduced all-cause mortality by 34% over 12 months (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.54-0.81). Hospitalization for heart failure also decreased by 27%. Bradycardia requiring dose reduction occurred in 9% of patients on carvedilol.
title: Carvedilol for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: mortality benefit
